content.content:
176	## Decided — copy model: phrase-carrying tokens (confirmed by Marcel 2026-09-12)
177	
178	**Tokens name a phrase, not a bare noun** — `{inCountry}`, not `{country}`.
179	
180	Reads identically in English, costs nothing now, and lets the copy author supply
181	*"in the United Kingdom"* or *"in Francia"* — **preposition included** — without anyone
182	touching the component or renaming a key. If the authors later prefer full per-locale
183	sentences instead, that also works: `interpolateUiCopy` leaves unmatched tokens in place, so
184	an unused token is harmless.
185	
186	**Why this matters:** French, Italian and Spanish inflect — *"di Francia"*, *"dell'Italia"*,
187	*"degli Emirati"* — so a bare `{country}` slot cannot be made grammatical. The design already
188	demonstrates the failure twice: row 3's CTA reads *"PASSA AL NEGOZIO SAN MARINO"* while its own
189	body correctly says *"al negozio **di** San Marino"* (preposition lost in substitution), and
190	row 2's reads *"SHIPSPEDISCI IN AUSTRALIA"* (an English and an Italian template fused).
191	
192	**What we currently implement** (surveyed 2026-09-12):
193	
194	| | State |
195	|---|---|
196	| Key convention | dot-path — `login.drawer.createAccount.heading`, `footer.copyright.label` |
197	| English fallback | always inline as `t()`'s 2nd arg; components work with zero Contentful |
198	| Interpolation machinery | exists — `{token}` regex in `interpolateUiCopy` (`useUiCopy.ts:21-24`) |
199	| Interpolation **in use** | **exactly once** — `list-menu-popover.tsx:228`, `'{name} menu'` |
200	| Seeded entries | 8 (SFCC-742), **all static**, **all English-only** (`value: { 'en': … }`) |
201	| Translated uiCopy values | **none anywhere in the project** |
202	
203	Note the one existing precedent (`'{name} menu'`) already carries this latent bug — `list-menu`
204	renders on the EU storefronts, where correct Italian is *"menu Abiti"*, not *"Abiti menu"*.
205	
206	**Key point that de-risked this:** SFCC-831's code is **identical under every inflection model**
207	— it just calls `t(key, fallback, values)`. Whether the value is `"France"` or `"in Francia"` is
208	the consumer's and copy author's decision. So this card only ever had to fix the *token names*.
209	
210	Proposed key set (8 keys, to be sanity-checked by whoever authors the copy):
211	
212	```
213	regional.locationPrompt.heading     "Looks like you're {inCountry}"
214	regional.locationPrompt.body        "You're currently shopping on {currentStore}. Switch to
215	                                     {targetStore} for local pricing, currency and shipping options."
216	regional.locationPrompt.cta.switch  "Switch to {targetStore}"
217	regional.locationPrompt.cta.stay    "Stay on {currentStore}"
218	regional.languagePrompt.heading     "Welcome to Zimmermann Europe"
219	regional.languagePrompt.body        "Welcome to Zimmermann Europe. We noticed you're {inCountry},
220	                                     would you like to view our site {inLanguage}?"
221	regional.languagePrompt.cta.switch  "View {inLanguage}"
222	regional.languagePrompt.cta.stay    "Continue {inCurrentLanguage}"
223	```
224	
225	The language body deliberately tracks REG-031's prescribed format (*"Welcome to Zimmermann
226	Europe — we noticed you're located in [detected country]"*). Every key also needs a
227	`description` for the TransPerfect translator, who works key-by-key with no view of the page —
228	the `uiCopy` content type's own comment says as much.
229	
230	**DECIDED (Marcel, 2026-09-12): ship derived fallbacks + a seed script. Copy is not a
231	dependency on the BA at all.**
232	
233	The templates above are **recoverable from the canonical design** — only the placeholder
234	*values* were incoherent (header says detected UK, body says *currently shopping* UK; both
235	can't be true or the panel wouldn't have opened). Every fallback is the design's own sentence
236	with the bad example values swapped for tokens. The language body is stronger still: it matches
237	**REG-031's prescribed format** (*"Welcome to Zimmermann Europe — we noticed you're located in
238	[detected country]"*), so it's the requirement, not a reading of the design.
239	
240	Two implementation details:
241	
242	1. **Store sentence case; let CSS uppercase.** `textStyle="heading3"` carries
243	   `textTransform: uppercase` and `ZimmButton` uppercases its own labels. So store
244	   `Looks like you're {inCountry}`, never `LOOKS LIKE YOU'RE …` — capitalisation rules differ
245	   by language, and a translator handed caps returns caps.
246	2. **The language variant repeats its welcome** — heading *"Zimmermann Europa ti dà il
247	   benvenuto"* and body opening *"Benvenuta/o su Zimmermann Europa…"*. Ship it faithfully; a
248	   copywriter will likely cut one, and that's a Contentful edit, not a deploy.
249	
250	**Also in scope: a seed script.** `scripts/contentful/seedRegionalPromptUiCopy.mjs`, modelled on
251	`seedLoginDrawerUiCopy.mjs` (~20 lines, idempotent, `--target <env>`), seeding the 8 keys with
252	English values **and** the `description` text.
253	
254	Why it's worth the 20 lines: every non-default Contentful locale is `optional: true` with
255	`fallbackCode: 'en'`, so **an un-authored translation renders in English silently** — no error,
256	no missing-key marker. For a feature whose whole point is REG-031 (*message in the language of
257	the current storefront URL*), that is the requirement failing invisibly. Seeding converts it
258	into a visible gap: eight entries sitting in the CMS with no Italian value, where the content
259	team actually works. The `description` field is load-bearing too — the `uiCopy` type's own
260	comment notes TransPerfect translators work key-by-key with no view of the page.
261	
262	Path is untiered: `scripts/contentful/` root is not in `protectedFiles.md` (only
263	`content-types/`, `buildTemplate.js` and `setup/installTemplate.mjs` are).
264	
265	---
266	
267	## Modal decision — revisited and re-confirmed (2026-09-12)
268

## Decided — copy model: phrase-carrying tokens (confirmed by Marcel 2026-09-12)

**Tokens name a phrase, not a bare noun** — `{inCountry}`, not `{country}`.

Reads identically in English, costs nothing now, and lets the copy author supply
*"in the United Kingdom"* or *"in Francia"* — **preposition included** — without anyone
touching the component or renaming a key. If the authors later prefer full per-locale
sentences instead, that also works: `interpolateUiCopy` leaves unmatched tokens in place, so
an unused token is harmless.

**Why this matters:** French, Italian and Spanish inflect — *"di Francia"*, *"dell'Italia"*,
*"degli Emirati"* — so a bare `{country}` slot cannot be made grammatical. The design already
demonstrates the failure twice: row 3's CTA reads *"PASSA AL NEGOZIO SAN MARINO"* while its own
body correctly says *"al negozio **di** San Marino"* (preposition lost in substitution), and
row 2's reads *"SHIPSPEDISCI IN AUSTRALIA"* (an English and an Italian template fused).

**What we currently implement** (surveyed 2026-09-12):

| | State |
|---|---|
| Key convention | dot-path — `login.drawer.createAccount.heading`, `footer.copyright.label` |
| English fallback | always inline as `t()`'s 2nd arg; components work with zero Contentful |
| Interpolation machinery | exists — `{token}` regex in `interpolateUiCopy` (`useUiCopy.ts:21-24`) |
| Interpolation **in use** | **exactly once** — `list-menu-popover.tsx:228`, `'{name} menu'` |
| Seeded entries | 8 (SFCC-742), **all static**, **all English-only** (`value: { 'en': … }`) |
| Translated uiCopy values | **none anywhere in the project** |

Note the one existing precedent (`'{name} menu'`) already carries this latent bug — `list-menu`
renders on the EU storefronts, where correct Italian is *"menu Abiti"*, not *"Abiti menu"*.

**Key point that de-risked this:** SFCC-831's code is **identical under every inflection model**
— it just calls `t(key, fallback, values)`. Whether the value is `"France"` or `"in Francia"` is
the consumer's and copy author's decision. So this card only ever had to fix the *token names*.

Proposed key set (8 keys, to be sanity-checked by whoever authors the copy):

```
regional.locationPrompt.heading     "Looks like you're {inCountry}"
regional.locationPrompt.body        "You're currently shopping on {currentStore}. Switch to
                                     {targetStore} for local pricing, currency and shipping options."
regional.locationPrompt.cta.switch  "Switch to {targetStore}"
regional.locationPrompt.cta.stay    "Stay on {currentStore}"
regional.languagePrompt.heading     "Welcome to Zimmermann Europe"
regional.languagePrompt.body        "Welcome to Zimmermann Europe. We noticed you're {inCountry},
                                     would you like to view our site {inLanguage}?"
regional.languagePrompt.cta.switch  "View {inLanguage}"
regional.languagePrompt.cta.stay    "Continue {inCurrentLanguage}"
```

The language body deliberately tracks REG-031's prescribed format (*"Welcome to Zimmermann
Europe — we noticed you're located in [detected country]"*). Every key also needs a
`description` for the TransPerfect translator, who works key-by-key with no view of the page —
the `uiCopy` content type's own comment says as much.

**DECIDED (Marcel, 2026-09-12): ship derived fallbacks + a seed script. Copy is not a
dependency on the BA at all.**

The templates above are **recoverable from the canonical design** — only the placeholder
*values* were incoherent (header says detected UK, body says *currently shopping* UK; both
can't be true or the panel wouldn't have opened). Every fallback is the design's own sentence
with the bad example values swapped for tokens. The language body is stronger still: it matches
**REG-031's prescribed format** (*"Welcome to Zimmermann Europe — we noticed you're located in
[detected country]"*), so it's the requirement, not a reading of the design.

Two implementation details:

1. **Store sentence case; let CSS uppercase.** `textStyle="heading3"` carries
   `textTransform: uppercase` and `ZimmButton` uppercases its own labels. So store
   `Looks like you're {inCountry}`, never `LOOKS LIKE YOU'RE …` — capitalisation rules differ
   by language, and a translator handed caps returns caps.
2. **The language variant repeats its welcome** — heading *"Zimmermann Europa ti dà il
   benvenuto"* and body opening *"Benvenuta/o su Zimmermann Europa…"*. Ship it faithfully; a
   copywriter will likely cut one, and that's a Contentful edit, not a deploy.

**Also in scope: a seed script.** `scripts/contentful/seedRegionalPromptUiCopy.mjs`, modelled on
`seedLoginDrawerUiCopy.mjs` (~20 lines, idempotent, `--target <env>`), seeding the 8 keys with
English values **and** the `description` text.

Why it's worth the 20 lines: every non-default Contentful locale is `optional: true` with
`fallbackCode: 'en'`, so **an un-authored translation renders in English silently** — no error,
no missing-key marker. For a feature whose whole point is REG-031 (*message in the language of
the current storefront URL*), that is the requirement failing invisibly. Seeding converts it
into a visible gap: eight entries sitting in the CMS with no Italian value, where the content
team actually works. The `description` field is load-bearing too — the `uiCopy` type's own
comment notes TransPerfect translators work key-by-key with no view of the page.

Path is untiered: `scripts/contentful/` root is not in `protectedFiles.md` (only
`content-types/`, `buildTemplate.js` and `setup/installTemplate.mjs` are).

---

## Modal decision — revisited and re-confirmed (2026-09-12)

Marcel reopened this on the grounds that it "isn't really a modal, just a drawer that isn't
full-page height." Checked, and **`ZimmDrawer` is modal by construction**, not incidentally:
`useModalContext()` → `getDialogProps()` (`role="dialog"` + `aria-modal`), `<ModalFocusScope>`
(focus trap), `zIndex: 'modal'`, dimmed overlay — and its own docblock names **body-scroll
lock** twice. The page behind cannot scroll, so panel height is irrelevant to modality. AC3's
required focus trap is independently modal behaviour: you cannot trap focus and permit browsing.

Going non-modal would need a new shell or a new mode on the shared atom, contradicts AC3/AC4,
and **wouldn't fix the Didomi collision anyway** — SFCC-823's country prompt fires on first
visit across 7 of 8 storefronts and is modal for the same reasons. Decision stands: **modal**.

**The reframe that came out of it.** Modal drawers are the pre-existing norm — all three current
consumers are modal. But **every modal in this app today opens because the shopper asked**
(`openPdpDrawerAtTab`, `openBoutiqueDrawerRaw`, the wishlist trigger); none opens on mount, and
the one thing that ever did — Salesforce's DNT placeholder — was removed by SFCC-863, which now
has a regression suite asserting it never renders. So **SFCC-823/689 would be this storefront's
first uninvited modal**, and Didomi its second. That is the genuinely new behaviour, and the
whole reason no precedence rule exists: there has never been anything to sequence.

---

## Out of scope for this build

- **First-visit modal precedence vs Didomi** — Marcel, explicit: *"not a consideration for this
  build."* Owned by SFCC-689/823, which hold the trigger logic; SFCC-831 renders when told and
  has no opinion on when. Recorded here only so it isn't lost: this app has no prior art for an
  uninvited modal, so the rule needs to cover queue-vs-suppress as well as ordering, and Didomi

## Review Findings — Step C3 (ZimmLanguagePrompt mount)

### 1. Structure (components.md) — CLEAN
All CONFIRMED: named export `ZimmLanguagePrompt` (index.tsx:102) matches folder `zimmLanguagePrompt/`; props type `ZimmLanguagePromptProps` (index.tsx:14) matches component name; `index.stories.tsx` and `index.test.tsx` both exist. Grep for `use[A-Z]\w*(` in index.tsx hits only `useEffect(` (line 109) and the JSDoc's prose mentions of `useMultiSite()` in comments — zero real hook calls to `useMultiSite`/`useCurrentBasket`/`useIntl`/`useUiCopy`. `useState` (line 103) and `useEffect` (line 109) are the only two hooks called. Site/locale/buildUrl are received as props exactly as `ZimmLanguagePromptProps` declares (index.tsx:14-21). 🔵 n/a (pass).

### 2. Imports — CLEAN
- **Circular import:** CONFIRMED none. Grepped `zimmLanguagePrompt` across `zimmCountryLanguageMismatch/`, `regionPrefCookie.ts`, `shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts`, `crossSiteUrl.ts` — the only hit is a **comment**, not an import (`zimmCountryLanguageMismatch/index.stories.tsx:61`, prose reference to "real use at zimmLanguagePrompt/index.tsx's EU_LANGUAGE_CONFIG map"). No `import ... from '...zimmLanguagePrompt'` anywhere in those four files.
- **`../../../..` depth:** CONFIRMED none — the 3 new files contain zero `../` relative imports at all; everything is either a package import, the `app/...` alias, or a single-level `./index`.
- **Base-path-standing-in-for-override rule:** CONFIRMED vacuous. Searched `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` for any country/region/language-mismatch base component — nothing exists (only an unrelated `use-sf-payments-country.js` hook). `ZimmCountryLanguageMismatch` is a wholly Zimmermann-original organism (its own doc comment says "modelled on `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx`"), so there is no SFCC base module being shadowed — overrideStyling.md's rule simply doesn't apply here.
- **Later-sprint reference:** CONFIRMED clean. `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` exists but is a stale June draft; irrelevant regardless since every dependency (`regionPrefCookie.ts`, `shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts`, `crossSiteUrl.ts`, `ZimmCountryLanguageMismatch`) is already committed on this branch (`b660d69`, `a89b8b3`, `fe8b1a4`, `2d4fac8` per git log) — nothing reaches into unbuilt work.

### 3. Accessibility — VACUOUS for this step's new code
CONFIRMED. Grepped all 3 new files for `<img`, `IconButton`, `onClick`: zero hits in `index.tsx` (it returns only `null` or `<ZimmCountryLanguageMismatch .../>`, no raw markup) and zero in `index.stories.tsx`. The only `onClick` hits are in `index.test.tsx:28-29`, on native `<button>` elements inside a test-only mock stub — natively interactive, no `role`/`tabIndex`/`onKeyDown` needed. This angle has nothing to check for this step's own diff.

### 4. Intra-step DRY — 2 real findings + 1 additional
- 🟡 **CONFIRMED, UNIFORM.** `const SITE = { id: 'ZimmermannEUit', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU' };` and `const LOCALE = { id: 'it' };` are byte-identical in `index.test.tsx:68-69` and `index.stories.tsx:29-30`, with no shared fixture module (verified — each file declares its own top-level `const`). A repo-wide scan (comparing every sibling `index.test.tsx`/`index.stories.tsx` pair for shared const-literal lines) found this exact duplication nowhere else today — so no live *sibling* instance exists yet — but the codebase has zero convention for sharing plain data fixtures between a test and its story (the `*Shared.ts` precedent — `footerShared.ts`, `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`, `zimmDrawerShared.ts`, `headerShared.ts` — is CSS/theme-values-only). The missing convention is systemic, so I judge this UNIFORM risk going forward, not a one-off oddity of this file pair.
- 🔵 **CONFIRMED, UNIFORM (lower severity, as requested).** The raw string `'ZimmermannEU'` is hardcoded at `index.test.tsx:68,116,130,153` and `index.stories.tsx:29`, instead of importing `EU_DOMESTIC_SFCC_SITE_ID` (exported at `shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts:10`). Same "magic string duplicating a named constant" shape could recur anywhere this site ID is referenced in a fixture.
- 🔵 **Additional, independently found.** `BUILD_URL` is redefined separately in both files — `index.test.tsx:70` (`vi.fn((path: string) => path)`) and `index.stories.tsx:31` (`(path: string): string => path`) — same no-op-identity fixture concept, not sharing a source. Not byte-identical code, so lower-grade than the SITE/LOCALE case, but the same missing-shared-fixture root cause.

### 5. Citation accuracy
- **(a) `regionPrefCookie.ts:55`** — CONFIRMED accurate. Line 55 is exactly `readonly countrySuppressedAt?: number;` inside `RegionPrefCookieValue`. I additionally verified the comment's stronger sub-claim ("has no production caller anywhere in this codebase yet") by grepping all of `overrides/` for `countrySuppressedAt`: it appears only in `regionPrefCookie.ts`'s own type/parse/serialise plumbing, `regionPrefCookie.test.ts`, and this step's own new `index.test.tsx:192,199` (a test fixture, not a caller). Clean. 🔵 (pass, not a finding).
- **(b) `LanguageDetectedEnglish` story** — CONFIRMED accurate. Exists at `zimmCountryLanguageMismatch/index.stories.tsx:114-123`, and its own comment (lines 106-113) states the "Ireland not UK, because ZimmermannUK already exists" reasoning near-verbatim to what `zimmLanguagePrompt/index.tsx:42-46` echoes. Clean.
- **(c) `regionPrefCookie.ts:122-125`** — CONFIRMED, and I judge it a **meaningfully imprecise citation**, not close-enough. Lines 122-125 are `serialiseRegionPrefCookie` (pure, no `document` reference — its own doc comment at line 119 says so explicitly); `setRegionPrefCookie`, the function actually named in the claim, is defined separately at lines 158-168 and is the only one that touches `document.cookie`. The stories.tsx prose ("`setRegionPrefCookie(value)` serialises **and writes** exactly the object it's given ... `regionPrefCookie.ts:122-125`") attributes both "serialises" and "writes" to a 4-line range that only ever does the serialise half and never executes a write. A reader opening those exact lines to verify "writes... no merge form" would find a differently-named function that never assigns `document.cookie`. The substantive claim ("no merge/clear form") does hold once you read the *correct* function (158-168), so this isn't a false claim about behavior — it's a wrong line-anchor for the function named in the sentence. 🟡, UNIFORM — citing a callee's lines while describing the caller's behavior is a generic slip that could recur anywhere in this codebase's heavily cross-referenced doc comments.
- Bonus (not asked, verified in passing): `config/sites.overlay.js:39-42` cited in `index.tsx:48` — CONFIRMED exact match, both line numbers and alias/locale values for all four EU-domestic sites line up perfectly with `EU_LANGUAGE_CONFIG`.

### 6. EU_LANGUAGE_CONFIG hardcoded-English phrase values — real, unaddressed gap
CONFIRMED via targeted grep: `EU_LANGUAGE_CONFIG`, `countryPhrase`, `languagePhrase`, and `target-site` produce **zero hits**, case-insensitive, in both `decisions.md` and `plan.md`. The "Decided — copy model: phrase-carrying tokens" section (`decisions.md:176-263`) only decided the **outer template token-naming convention** (`{inCountry}` vs `{country}`) so a copy author can later supply a fully-inflected, per-locale phrase ("in Francia") without touching code — it never discusses, and was written before, this step's specific implementation choice (in `zimmLanguagePrompt/index.tsx:53-58`) to hardcode the phrase *values* themselves as permanent English string literals in application source, with no Contentful/locale sourcing path at all.

This sets up exactly the fused-language failure the same document calls out as a live example: `decisions.md:203-204` states the one existing `interpolateUiCopy` precedent (`list-menu-popover.tsx:228`, `'{name} menu'` — confirmed still present verbatim) "already carries this latent bug" on EU storefronts. The moment any EU locale gets a real Contentful translation for `regional.languagePrompt.body`/`heading` (currently zero exist — `decisions.md:201`, "Translated uiCopy values: none anywhere in the project"), the surrounding sentence will render in Italian/French/Spanish while `inCountry`/`inLanguage` stay frozen English, reproducing the documented "SHIPSPEDISCI IN AUSTRALIA" bug class (`decisions.md:190`) — directly undermining REG-031's stated goal ("message in the language of the current storefront URL," `decisions.md:256-257`).

Verdict: **real, currently-invisible-but-latent defect, not a signed-off scope boundary.** It is not on plan.md's 13-item open-questions list either (checked all 13; none mention `EU_LANGUAGE_CONFIG`, phrase-value localization, or this failure mode). 🟡 (invisible today only because zero locales are translated anywhere in the app; not a blocker for this PR, but nobody has decided it's acceptable — it should get its own tracked follow-up, the same way copy sign-off got open item #8). UNIFORM — the codebase already demonstrates this exact defect shape in a second, independent, already-shipped location.

### 7. Against the ticket (plan.md Step C3, lines 491-561)
Verified against the actual diff, not just narrative:

| Criterion | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `_app/index.tsx` diff ≤3 real lines | `git diff -U0`: exactly 2 added lines (import at old-line-55, JSX at old-line-484), 0 removed | CONFIRMED, well within budget |
| SFCC-863 suite unmodified, additive-only diff | `git diff` on `_app/index.test.tsx`: two hunks, both pure insertions (new `vi.mock` block + new `describe`/`test` block appended); zero lines touched in the existing DNT assertions | CONFIRMED |
| SFCC-885 suite unmodified | Same diff — that describe block is untouched | CONFIRMED |
| New positive mount assertion | `_app/index.test.tsx:298-314` | CONFIRMED |
| Container test's 4 core behaviors (null-render / Italian+Spanish resolution / cookie-before-navigate ordering / onDismiss) | `index.test.tsx:100-106, 125-167, 171-188, 216-230` — the ordering assertion genuinely compares `mock.invocationCallOrder` (not just "both were called") | CONFIRMED present and structurally sound |
| `useMultiSite` mocked via factory wherever used | `_app/index.test.tsx:142-148` (pre-existing factory); n/a to `zimmLanguagePrompt`'s own test since it takes props, not the hook | CONFIRMED |
| tsc / full 82-file test run / lint / audit:tokens counts | Not independently re-run — outside this review's read-only scope | UNVERIFIED by me (not a finding, a scope limit) |

**New finding, not on the open-questions list:** `index.test.tsx:184`'s comment cites "the SFCC-831/689 build report for this step" as the record of the mandatory red-then-green proof for the cookie-before-navigate ordering assertion (plan.md:544-547's "Mandatory sub-step"). I checked the only build-report-shaped artifact, `handoff.md`: its Steps table (lines 9-22) has rows for A1-A6, B1, B1a, B2, C1, C2 — **no C3 row at all**. Its own "Outstanding" section (line 94) still lists "Steps C2/C3 ... not yet started" even though C2 is separately recorded PASS two lines earlier — i.e., that section is stale, not a reliable current-state signal either way. More pointedly, `handoff.md:86`'s own "UNIFORM findings" section explicitly names **"C3's 'cookie-before-navigate ordering'"** as a self-report that "should be re-run by whoever scores them, not accepted as written" — the project's own prior audit already flagged this exact claim as unverified. I could not find the red-then-green record the test file cites anywhere. The assertion itself reads as well-built (real ordering comparison, not a weaker "both happened" check), so this is about unverified process/traceability, not a suspected functional bug. 🟡, UNIFORM (a build-report citation outrunning the actual record is a sequencing risk that could recur at any step).
